policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R2. If the application does not mention leaving a job, assume no member quit one in the past 30 days.
R3. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.
R4. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R5. If no member's age or disability is given, assume no member is 60 or older or disabled.
R6. No member may be a fleeing felon or a parole violator.
R7. Every member applying must give a Social Security number or proof of applying for one.
R8. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days. This rule does not apply if the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R9. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
case_text: Case file 1833 was opened by Linda Svensson this month. The total countable resources from bank accounts, stocks, and bonds are $2,900. The adult has accumulated 0 months of benefits without meeting work requirements over the past three years. During the intake process, the applicant inquired about expediting the appointment. Official records confirm the applicant has 40 qualifying work quarters. Social Security numbers have been provided for all applicants. The calculated net monthly income stands at $3,212 following all deductions. The applicant is a green card holder for more than 5 years. There are 5 individuals residing together and purchasing food as a single household. The household includes an individual who is 67 years of age. The household met all criteria to qualify for benefits prior to the strike. Monthly unearned income totals $600 through sources including Social Security and child support. The applicant is 52 years old, able-bodied, and resides in a home with no children under the age of 14. Employment records indicate a member left a position within the past 30 days under good cause due to documented workplace discrimination. No household members receive benefits through TANF or SSI. Monthly expenses for rent and utilities amount to $1,200. The shelter costs surpass half of the adjusted income by $-406. The household has no member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college. Documentation indicates the adult completes 120 hours monthly in employment or job training activities. The record shows no active warrants or parole violations for any household member. There are no recorded intentional program violations for the household. Income after applying the earned income and standard deductions is $3,212. Monthly earned income from wages totals $3,600. The client mentioned being a regular attendee at a local place of worship. A household member is presently participating in a labor strike at a manufacturing plant. The household maintains residency in the state where the application was filed. Combining earned and unearned revenue results in a gross monthly income of $4,200.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line.
R2. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R3. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R4. If the application does not mention college enrollment, assume no member is a college student.
R5. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible, unless the student works at least 20 hours a week.
R6. Every member applying must give a Social Security number or proof of applying for one.
R7. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month.
R8. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
case_text: Case file review for the assistance application submitted by Maria Gonzalez for fiscal year 2027. The applicant currently holds a temporary work visa according to immigration documentation. The family maintains their primary residence in an adjacent state rather than the jurisdiction of application. Monthly unearned income disbursements totaling $300 are received from sources including Social Security and child support. During the intake process, the applicant mentioned feeling uneasy about seeking public assistance for the first time. The household has a member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college who also works at least 20 hours a week. A total of 4 individuals reside together and share cooking arrangements. Inquiries were made regarding the possibility of expediting the scheduled appointment time. Employment history documentation reflects fewer than 40 qualifying work quarters. No cash assistance benefits from TANF or Supplemental Security Income are received by the household. Valid Social Security numbers have been provided for all household members. Employment records indicate a resignation within the past 30 days due to verified workplace discrimination. A household member is presently participating in a labor strike at a manufacturing plant. Combined earned and unearned revenue streams result in a gross monthly income of $2,100. Combined monthly expenses for housing rent and utility services amount to $1,200. Housing expenditures surpass fifty percent of adjusted income by an amount of $445. The adults in the home bear parental responsibility for a dependent child under the age of 14. State databases indicate an active disqualification for a member due to a previous program violation. Employment wages generate $1,800 per month for the household. The designated adult has utilized 2 months of assistance within the preceding three-year period without fulfilling work requirements. Law enforcement databases show no outstanding warrants or parole violations for any household member. The household met all criteria prior to the onset of the work stoppage. Income calculation following the deduction of earned wages and standard allowances totals $1,511. The individual is documented to perform 20 hours monthly of employment or approved training. Liquid assets held in checking and savings accounts sum to $3,100.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R2. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R3. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation.
R4. If the application does not mention leaving a job, assume no member quit one in the past 30 days.
R5. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R6. If the application does not show eligibility before a strike, assume the household was not eligible.
R7. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R8. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
R9. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days.
R2. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R3. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled.
R4. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R5. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation.
R6. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R7. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month, unless that adult has received benefits for fewer than 3 months of the past 36 without meeting this rule.
R8. If the application does not mention leaving a job, assume no member quit one in the past 30 days.

The calculated income following the application of earned income and standard deductions stands at $1,343. The roster contains no individuals aged 60 or older, nor anyone meeting disability criteria. Liquid assets including depository accounts, securities, and bonds amount to $4,000 in liquid wealth. During intake, the applicant inquired if the scheduled interview timeframe could be expedited. One household participant is currently participating in a labor strike at an industrial manufacturing facility. Employment records indicate that the applicant has accumulated 40 qualifying quarters of covered work. Background checks confirm no active status as a fleeing felon or any parole violations among members. The applicant expressed initial reluctance and noted a sense of personal discomfort regarding public assistance. Wage documentation from employment verification stubs indicates monthly earnings of $1,200. Combining all earned wages and unearned receipts results in a cumulative monthly gross income of $1,800. Every resident individual within the household currently receives Supplemental Security Income benefits. The designated adult has utilized 2 months of food assistance allotments during the preceding three-year timeframe without fulfilling standard work requirements. Following the subtraction of all allowable deductions, the final net monthly income figure is recorded at $1,343. Computed shelter expenses exceed fifty percent of the adjusted income by a margin of $-71. All participation criteria were successfully satisfied by the household on the calendar day preceding the labor strike. The physical residence of the applicant family is established within the boundaries of the filing state. No history of intentional program violations is documented in the administrative history of the household. The domestic unit consists of 2 members who jointly purchase provisions and prepare meals together. The subject adult maintains 120 hours per month in employment activities or approved work training programs. Valid Social Security numbers are officially documented for every applying individual. Review of recent employment history reveals a member separated from a job within the past 30 days due to documented workplace discrimination constituting good cause. Monthly unearned revenue derived from assistance payments and financial support totals $600. The applicant resides in the country under the terms of a temporary employment authorization visa.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.
R2. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled.
R3. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R4. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R5. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R6. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation, unless the applicant is a green card holder with 40 qualifying quarters of work.
R7. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R8. If qualifying work quarters are not documented, assume fewer than 40.
case_text: Case 6460 documents the SNAP application submitted by Keisha Johnson on behalf of their household for fiscal year 2027. The household includes a member between the ages of 18 and 49 who is enrolled in college at least half-time and is the primary caregiver for their own child under the age of six. Submitted pay records indicate that the household brings in $3,000 per month from employment. Background checks confirm that no individual in the household is currently classified as a fleeing felon or in violation of probation or parole terms. Official Social Security administration records verify that the applicant has accumulated a total of 40 qualifying quarters of work history. Total allowable shelter expenses surpass fifty percent of the adjusted income calculation by an amount of $-346. During intake, the applicant mentioned that this is their first time seeking public assistance and expressed feelings of embarrassment. The home contains no able-bodied adults who are residing without a young child dependent. Records indicate that during the preceding 36-month period, the adult received benefits for 1 months while failing to fulfill standard work requirements. Combining all earned and unearned revenue streams results in a total gross monthly income figure of $4,000. Employment history shows that a household member voluntarily left a job within the last 30 days specifically due to verified workplace discrimination, constituting good cause. The household receives neither Supplemental Security Income nor Temporary Assistance for Needy Families cash benefits. Prior to the labor strike event, the household's overall financial intake exceeded the threshold for program qualification. The applicant mentioned attending services at a local church on weekends. At least one person residing in the home is currently receiving government-administered disability benefits. None of the household participants are currently participating in a labor strike. Liquid assets including checking accounts, savings, stocks, and bonds total $2,900 in countable resources. The domestic unit consists of 6 individuals who routinely purchase and prepare their meals together. The adult member maintains employment or participates in an approved work activity for 20 hours a month. Following the application of all permitted deductions, the net monthly income stands at $3,092. The family currently resides in an adjacent state rather than the jurisdiction where they submitted this application. Review of the state database reveals no history of intentional program violations associated with any household member. The applicant inquired whether the assigned caseworker could expedite the processing of the interview. One of the applying individuals has failed to supply a valid Social Security number or documentation showing an application for one was made. Combined housing and utility expenses obligate the household to pay $1,200 monthly. After subtracting both the earned income deduction and the standard deduction, the remaining income is $3,092. The intake worker noted in the file that the applicant was cooperative, polite, and thoroughly prepared with documents. The household receives $1,000 every month in unearned income derived from support payments and benefit disbursements.

A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R2. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation.
R3. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R4. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R5. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month.
R6. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R7. If no disqualification is on record, assume no member is disqualified.
R8. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
case_text: Case file 6699 details the application submitted by Robert Kowalski for nutrition assistance. The household incurs combined monthly rent and utility expenses totaling $1,200. Employment earnings for the household register at $3,600 each month. Income calculation after applying the standard and earned income deductions results in $2,963. During the intake process, the applicant inquired about expediting the interview schedule. The working adult logs 80 hours monthly in employment or approved training activities. As for college enrollment, there is a member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college who also works at least 20 hours a week. Records indicate the adult received 3 months of benefits during the previous 36-month window without fulfilling work requirements. The applicant household currently resides within the boundaries of the filing state. There are no recorded intentional program violations or associated disqualifications for any individual. Employment history notes that a member left a position within the last 30 days due to verified workplace discrimination. Background checks confirm no individual holds status as a fleeing felon or parole violator. Liquid assets held in checking and savings accounts amount to $4,000 for the household. Community involvement for the applicant includes regular attendance at a nearby religious institution. Labor dispute records show one household member is currently participating in a factory strike. The family currently receives monthly cash assistance through the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program. Combining all earned and unearned revenue streams yields a gross monthly income of $3,900. All requested verification documents were successfully provided at the time of the interview. Medical documentation verifies that a household member is currently receiving disability benefits. The calculation of shelter expenses relative to half of the adjusted income yields $-281. In their free time, a member contributes volunteer hours at a local food distribution center. The household composition contains no able-bodied adults without dependent minor children. Unearned financial support from benefits and assistance payments totals $300 per month. A total of 2 individuals reside together and share food preparation arrangements. Program eligibility was already established and active prior to the initiation of the strike. Administration records accredit the applicant with 40 qualifying quarters of employment history. Valid Social Security numbers are documented for every individual listed on the application. The final net monthly income available after all allowable deductions is $2,963.

Combined earned and unearned revenue streams result in a gross monthly income of $4,600. Employment documentation verifies 40 hours a month of work or job training for that adult. The individual has utilized 0 months of benefits in the past three years without fulfilling the work requirement. A statewide database check indicates no intentional program violation is on record for the household. Housing expenditures, including rent and utility allowances, amount to $300 monthly. The final calculations establish a net monthly income of $3,651 after all allowable deductions. Prior to the labor dispute, the household's income level precluded qualification. Submitted employment verification records indicate monthly earnings of $3,600. The domestic unit consists of 4 members who share food purchasing and preparation habits. During the intake appointment, the client inquired about expediting the processing timeline. Law enforcement databases show no warrants or parole violations are on record for the household. System records confirm that every member of the household receives SSI. The adults in the household are currently caring for a child under 14. Subtracting the earned income and standard deductions leaves an adjusted income of $3,651. Department of Homeland Security records show the applicant is a Cuban or Haitian entrant. case_text: Case file 6227 documents the food assistance application submitted by James Carter for the household. A member aged 18 to 49 is enrolled at least half-time in college while also caring for their own child under 6. An active warrant indicates that one household member is currently fleeing to avoid prosecution for a felony. The interviewing caseworker noted that the applicant was cooperative, polite, and thoroughly prepared. Current pay stubs verify monthly earned income of $3,600. Official immigration documentation confirms the applicant holds citizenship in a Compact of Free Association nation, specifically the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, or Palau. Employment records establish that the applicant has accumulated 40 qualifying work quarters. Over the preceding 36 months, the adult received food assistance for 3 months without fulfilling the standard work requirement. Following the application of all allowable deductions, the calculated net monthly income stands at $3,458. No individual within the household carries any prior program violation disqualification. The adult members in the home are primarily responsible for caring for a child under the age of 14. Combining all earned and unearned revenue streams results in a gross monthly income of $4,600. Verified time logs demonstrate that the adult completes 80 hours a month of active employment or approved job training. Combined monthly expenses for rent and essential utilities total $1,900 for the household. Total shelter costs exceed fifty percent of the adjusted income threshold by $114. Every household member is under the age of 60, and no one is classified as disabled. A member of the household has actively participated in a labor strike since the preceding month. Unearned income derived from regular benefits and support payments totals $1,000 per month. Liquid assets held in checking and savings accounts comprise countable resources totaling $4,700. Review of recent employment history indicates a member voluntarily left a job within the past 30 days due to documented workplace discrimination, constituting good cause. No individual in the household currently receives benefits from TANF or SSI. After subtracting the earned income percentage and the standard deduction, the remaining income is $3,572. The domestic unit consists of 6 individuals who routinely purchase and prepare their meals together. The household failed to meet qualification criteria on the calendar day immediately preceding the labor strike. Valid Social Security numbers are officially documented for every applying individual. During off-hours, one member regularly volunteers at the local community food bank. The applicant participates in weekly community services at a nearby church.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Every member applying must give a Social Security number or proof of applying for one.
R2. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation.
R3. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R4. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible, unless the student works at least 20 hours a week.
R5. If no member's age or disability is given, assume no member is 60 or older or disabled.
R6. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line.
R7. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days. This rule does not apply if the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R8. If the application does not mention college enrollment, assume no member is a college student.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R2. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible.
R3. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R4. If the application does not mention college enrollment, assume no member is a college student.
R5. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days. This rule does not apply if the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R6. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R7. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line. This rule does not apply if a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R8. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation.

R1. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R2. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R3. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R4. If the application does not mention college enrollment, assume no member is a college student.
R5. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled.
R6. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible. This rule does not apply if the student works at least 20 hours a week.
R7. No member may be a fleeing felon or a parole violator.
R8. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month, unless that adult has received benefits for fewer than 3 months of the past 36 without meeting this rule.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R2. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.
R3. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R4. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled.
R5. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R6. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R7. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation. This rule does not apply if the applicant is a green card holder with 40 qualifying quarters of work.
R8. If qualifying work quarters are not documented, assume fewer than 40.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. No member may be a fleeing felon or a parole violator.
R2. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R3. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month.
R4. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
R5. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line. This rule does not apply if a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R6. If no warrant or parole violation is on record, assume no member is a fleeing felon or parole violator.
R7. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible. This rule does not apply if the student works at least 20 hours a week.
R8. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
R2. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.
R3. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible.
R4. No member may be a fleeing felon or a parole violator.
R5. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days. This rule does not apply if the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R6. If the application does not show eligibility before a strike, assume the household was not eligible.
R7. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R8. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days. This rule does not apply if the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R2. A member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college is not eligible.
R3. No member may be a fleeing felon or a parole violator.
R4. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R5. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line.
R6. The household must live in the state where it applies.
R7. No member may be serving a disqualification for an intentional program violation.
R8. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R9. If no member's age or disability is given, assume no member is 60 or older or disabled.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled, unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI.
R2. If the application does not mention leaving a job, assume no member quit one in the past 30 days.
R3. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R4. The household must live in the state where it applies.
R5. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R6. Every member applying must give a Social Security number or proof of applying for one.
R7. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R8. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line.
R9. An able-bodied adult aged 18 to 64 with no child under 14 in the household must work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month.
case_text: Case record for application 1319 submitted by Keisha Johnson. Documentation confirms a household member left employment within the prior 30 days due to verified workplace discrimination. The household contains no able-bodied adults without dependents. There are no recorded program violation disqualifications for any individual in the home. Five individuals reside together and purchase and prepare their meals collectively. Verifications show liquid assets totaling $4,000 in checking, savings, and investments. The calculated net monthly income stands at $-1,402 after all allowable deductions. Monthly employment earnings for the group equal $0. An adult member received assistance for 6 months during the preceding 36-month period without fulfilling standard work hours. Housing and utility expenses amount to $1,900 on a monthly basis. The housing expenses surpass 50 percent of the adjusted income by $1,734. No assistance is received through Temporary Assistance for Needy Families or Supplemental Security Income. The adult member logs 79 monthly hours in employment or qualifying training activities. No outstanding felony warrants or probation violations appear in records for any applicant. The group receives $600 each month from government benefits and support payments. Combining all revenue sources results in a gross monthly total of $600. The adjusted figure is $332 following the application of standard and earned income deductions. The client inquired about expediting the eligibility interview. The household includes one member who is 67 years of age. All requested verification paperwork was submitted by the client at the appointment. A participant regularly contributes time to a community food pantry. Federal earnings records verify 40 qualifying quarters of work for the applicant. The applicant expressed reluctance in seeking assistance for the first time. The applicant holds refugee status and currently lacks a permanent resident card. The family maintains their primary residence within the filing jurisdiction. The household met all criteria for assistance prior to the onset of the labor stoppage. None of the residents are currently participating in a strike. As for college enrollment, there is a member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college who also works at least 20 hours a week.

policy_text:
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): household eligibility rules, fiscal year 2027
A household is approved only if it meets every rule below. Income figures are monthly. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the application is silent on a point.

R1. The household is not eligible if a member quit a job in the past 30 days, unless the member left the job for good cause, such as discrimination, a required move, or caring for a family member.
R2. A household with a member on strike is eligible only if it was eligible on the day before the strike began.
R3. If the application does not show TANF or SSI, treat the household as not receiving either.
R4. Countable resources may not exceed $3,000, or $4,750 if a member is 60 or older or disabled.
R5. Gross monthly income (earned plus unearned) may not exceed $1,729 for a 1-person household plus $616 for each additional member, which is 130% of the poverty line, unless a member is aged 60 or older or disabled.
R6. Unless the household receives TANF cash assistance or SSI, net monthly income may not exceed $1,330 for a 1-person household plus $474 for each additional member. Net income is gross income minus 20% of earned income, minus a standard deduction ($217 for 1 to 3 members, $229 for 4, $268 for 5, $308 for 6), minus shelter costs above half of the income left after those deductions (that shelter deduction is capped at $769 unless a member is 60 or older or disabled).
R7. The applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a green card holder of more than 5 years, a Cuban or Haitian entrant, or a citizen of a Compact of Free Association nation. This rule does not apply if the applicant is a green card holder with 40 qualifying quarters of work.
R8. If qualifying work quarters are not documented, assume fewer than 40.
case_text: Case file 5856 was initiated by Maria Gonzalez during the current filing period. Law enforcement databases confirm no active warrants or probation infractions exist for any resident. Assistance and support distributions provide the home with $600 in monthly unearned revenue. The family resides across the border in an adjacent state rather than the jurisdiction of application. Primary caregivers in the domestic unit are directly responsible for a minor under the age of 14. Liquid assets held across depository accounts equal $800. During the intake appointment, the primary filer displayed exemplary cooperation and organization. Assessment confirms the domicile failed to meet qualification thresholds immediately preceding the labor disruption. Employment tracking documents verify 80 monthly hours dedicated to active employment or vocational instruction. Immigration records show the applicant is a green card holder for less than 5 years. Combined employment earnings and secondary receipts total $4,200 in gross monthly revenue. The claimant expressed initial apprehension regarding seeking public assistance for the first time. Applying standard exemptions and employment subtractions leaves an adjusted revenue figure of $3,212. All requested verification paperwork was meticulously compiled and presented by the applicant. Community involvement includes regular volunteer shifts at a regional charitable pantry. The household has a member aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in college who cares for their own child under 6. Final calculations establish a net monthly revenue of $3,212 following all applicable deductions. None of the individuals listed are currently participating in organized work stoppages. Medical documentation verifies that a member qualifies for government-administered disability compensation. The individual received benefits for 6 months outside standard participation terms within the prior 36-month window. Agency records show zero history of fraudulent infractions or program policy violations. Five individuals share a common domicile and jointly purchase and prepare their daily meals. No residents currently draw support from supplemental security or family assistance programs. Federal employment archives attribute 40 qualifying quarters of covered labor to the applicant. Valid identification numbers issued by the Social Security Administration are verified for all participants. Employment records confirm a voluntary departure from a previous position within the last 30 days due to verified workplace discrimination. Monthly employment wages received by the domestic unit amount to $3,600. Housing expenditures surpass 50 percent of the adjusted financial baseline by $-106. Housing obligations, including dwelling rent and utility services, require $1,500 per month.
